title: Introduce request-phase attribution, interleaved span annotator, and cascade alert suppression
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Long-running incidents showed noisy alert storms when fallback/replicate paths triggered cascades and retries. Teams need per-request phase attribution (parse/routing/kernels/streaming) and trace-level stitching across retries to correctly attribute latency and token cost, plus a way to suppress alert storms that are a result of one upstream failure. This PR implements three coordinated changes: 1) request-phase attribution metricization: add phase timers and token-cost counters at each logical phase (ingest, routing, kv-cache, kernel-exec, streaming) emitted as low-cardinality labels that can be aggregated; 2) interleaved-span annotator: a tracing library component that synthesizes stable span anchors (synthetic_parent_id & phase_id) and stitches retry/fallback spans into a single logical request view for UI rollups; 3) cascade alert suppression: a server-side alert dampener that detects correlated spike patterns originating from the same upstream invocation fingerprint and suppresses secondary alerts for a bounded window (configurable per-tenant). The description below summarizes changes, testing, rollout, and follow-ups.
Changes: - serving/runtime/phase_attribution: new Go package that records phase start/stop timings and token counters. Exposes metrics via Prometheus histogram + OTLP span attributes. - tracing/annotator: interleaved-span annotator middleware (Go) that injects synthetic_parent_id and phase_id into spans and emits compact SpanAnchor events for the trace collector. - observability/metrics: new metric names (redwood_request_phase_seconds_bucket, redwood_request_phase_tokens_total, redwood_request_phase_error_count) and a migration doc mapping old token/latency metrics. - console/dashboards: added "Request Phase Waterfall" dashboard (JSON panel) with stacked latency and token-cost heatmap keyed by phase and model_variant. - alerts/cascade_suppressor: new component (Rust) that subscribes to alert events and enforces suppression policy using fingerprint indices with a TTL-backed bloom filter for memory efficiency. - docs: docs/observability/phase_attribution.md with recommended dashboards and SLO considerations. - tests: integration and e2e tests covering phase metrics under normal/fallback flows and a synthetic incident replay harness to validate suppression heuristics.
Implementation notes: - Metrics are emitted with low-cardinality labels: phase, model_variant, region, tenant_id (hashed for privacy). High-cardinality route and prompt tags are intentionally excluded from the base metrics; route-level rollups are handled by the console joiner. - Annotator uses a lightweight deterministic fingerprint (sha1 of first-3-kv cache keys + model hash + timestamp bucket) so it is stable across retries but inexpensive to compute. - Suppressor uses a windowed token-decay heuristic (suppression window default 90s) and a configurable aggressiveness score; default policy is conservative to avoid hiding unique failures.
Testing & CI: - Unit tests for phase timers, annotated spans, and suppression decision logic. - Integration tests run against local runtimes simulating fallback chains (primary -> model-fallback -> region-fallback). - Bench: microbench shows annotator adds ~120ns/span on p99 and metrics emission is batched to avoid syscall overhead. - CI: initial integration CI failed intermittently due to a flaky test (retry ordering); fixed by adding deterministic seed in test harness.
Rollout plan: - Canary: enable metrics+annotator for 5% of traffic for internal tenants for two weeks; monitor heatmap and trace stitching accuracy. - Suppressor: start in passive monitoring mode (no suppression) for one week to gather baseline correlations; then opt-in aggressive suppression for internal tenants, followed by gradual tenant rollout. - Feature flags to toggle per-tenant: phase_metrics, annotator_inject, cascade_suppressor_mode.
Review notes: reviewers asked for privacy constraints on tenant labels (hashing implemented), and for an escape hatch to disable suppression per-route (added). Related work: follow-up ENG-3478 to add UI controls for suppression tuning in Console, and ENG-3502 to surface phase-level cost at the token-aggregation API. Backwards compatibility: metric names are additive and the annotator preserves existing span ids; no breaking changes. Migration: small migration doc included recommending alert rule tweaks and new dashboard templates.
